chapter_title: What Did They Study in Wuhan?

sources.author: Yount, Boyd, et al.
sources.title: Systematic assembly of a full-length infectious cDNA of mouse hepatitis virus strain A59
sources.summary: Baric-lab 2002 JVI paper on assembling a full-length infectious cDNA of mouse hepatitis virus—early synthetic coronavirus reverse-genetics platform. PubMed scrape failed.
sources.book_role: Opens Baric’s trajectory: creating synthetic coronavirus clones in the lab (chapter notes).

sources.author: Roberts, Anjeanette, et al.
sources.title: A Mouse-Adapted SARS-Coronavirus Causes Disease and Mortality in BALB/c Mice
sources.summary: 2007 PLOS Pathogens study creating a mouse-adapted SARS-CoV that causes disease and mortality in BALB/c mice via serial passage—lab evolution of pathogenicity.
sources.book_role: Baric-lineage work adapting SARS-CoV-1 in mice—step two of the research trajectory Chapter 12 traces.

sources.author: Becker, Michelle, et al.
sources.title: Synthetic recombinant bat SARS-like coronavirus is infectious in cultured cells and in mice
sources.summary: 2008 PNAS paper on a synthetic recombinant bat SARS-like coronavirus infectious in cells and mice—spike/backbone chimera work in the Baric orbit.
sources.book_role: Shows insertion of SARS spike into a synthetic backbone—bridging bat CoV genetics and mammalian infection (chapter notes).

sources.author: Li, Wendong, et al.
sources.title: Bats are natural reservoirs of SARS-like coronaviruses
sources.summary: 2005 Science paper establishing horseshoe bats as natural reservoirs of SARS-like coronaviruses—foundational for Shi Zhengli’s subsequent WIV program.
sources.book_role: Starts Shi’s research trajectory Chapter 12 maps: bats as SARS-like CoV reservoirs.

sources.author: Jacobsen, Rowan
sources.title: Inside the risky bat-virus engineering that links America to Wuhan
sources.summary: MIT Technology Review deep dive on gain-of-function bat-virus engineering linking U.S. labs (Baric/EcoHealth) to Wuhan, including WIV1 reverse genetics under lower biosafety.
sources.book_role: Narrative bridge explaining how American and Wuhan bat-virus engineering programs connected.

sources.author: Butler, Declan
sources.title: Engineered bat virus stirs debate over risky research
sources.summary: 2015 Nature news on the Menachery/Baric/Shi chimeric bat SARS-like virus paper that stirred gain-of-function debate over risky research.
sources.book_role: Contemporaneous alarm at engineered bat–SARS chimeras—the controversy Chapter 12 revisits.

sources.author: Ren, Wuze, et al.
sources.title: Difference in Receptor Usage Between Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS) Coronavirus and SARS-Like Coronavirus of Bat Origin
sources.summary: 2008 JVI Shi-associated paper on receptor-usage differences; chapter notes: chimeric spikes showed bat SARS-like CoVs could be modified to infect human cells. PubMed scrape failed.
sources.book_role: Documents WIV capability to retarget bat CoV spikes toward human cells.

sources.author: Hou, Yuxuan, et al.
sources.title: Angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) proteins of different bat species confer variable susceptibility to SARS-CoV entry
sources.summary: 2010 Archives of Virology study testing ACE2 from different bat species for variable SARS-CoV entry susceptibility—mapping which bat receptors allow infection.
sources.book_role: Shows WIV systematically probing bat ACE2 compatibility with SARS entry.

sources.author: Zeng, Lei-Ping, et al.
sources.title: Bat Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome-Like Coronavirus WIV1 Encodes an Extra Accessory Protein, ORFX, Involved in Modulation of the Host Immune Response
sources.summary: 2016 JVI paper on WIV1 infectious clone and ORFX mutants—reverse-genetics platform later cited in DIA analysis; experiments under BSL-2 per chapter notes. PubMed scrape failed.
sources.book_role: Marks WIV’s live bat CoV infectious-clone capability—central to ‘what they studied in Wuhan.’

sources.author: Hu, Ben, et al.
sources.title: Discovery of a rich gene pool of bat SARS-related coronaviruses provides new insights into the origin of SARS coronavirus
sources.summary: 2017 PLoS Pathogens Hu et al.: rich Yunnan-cave gene pool of bat SARS-related CoVs; native and chimeric viruses infect human cells—direct WIV lab characterization of spillover-capable viruses.
sources.book_role: Shows WIV isolating and chimera-testing human-cell-infecting bat SARSr-CoVs from Yunnan caves.

sources.author: Zhou, Peng, et al.
sources.title: Fatal swine acute diarrhoea syndrome caused by an HKU2-related coronavirus of bat origin
sources.summary: 2018 Nature Zhou et al. on SADS: fatal swine acute diarrhoea from an HKU2-related bat coronavirus—WIV work infecting piglets with a bat CoV (chapter notes).
sources.book_role: Documents WIV moving from cell work to infecting livestock with bat coronaviruses.

sources.author: Lin, Christina
sources.title: Why US outsourced bat virus research to Wuhan
sources.summary: Asia Times piece on why U.S. entities outsourced bat-virus research to Wuhan. Only a browser-check interstitial was retrieved.
sources.book_role: Frames the U.S.–Wuhan outsourcing politics around the research Chapter 12 catalogs.

sources.title: Understanding the Risk of Bat Coronavirus Emergence
sources.summary: NIH RePORTER record for EcoHealth/Daszak R01AI110964 bat-coronavirus emergence grant—funding link reused from chapter 10 scrape cache.
sources.book_role: The NIAID grant tying U.S. money to the Wuhan bat-CoV agenda Chapter 12 inventories.

sources.author: Hu, Ben, et al.
sources.title: Discovery of a rich gene pool of bat SARS-related coronaviruses provides new insights into the origin of SARS coronavirus
sources.summary: DOI twin of Hu et al. 2017 PLoS Pathogens Yunnan SARSr-CoV gene-pool paper (same study as s10).
sources.book_role: Alternate citation path for the same rich gene-pool / chimera findings.

sources.title: Dr. Fauci, CDC Director Testify Before Senate on COVID-19 Guidelines
sources.summary: Rev transcript of May 11, 2021 Senate testimony including Fauci’s exchange on NIH funding and gain-of-function research linked to Wuhan.
sources.book_role: Primary transcript of the Rand Paul–Fauci GoF confrontation Chapter 12’s notes discuss.

sources.title: Complete Heated Exchange between Sen. Rand Paul and Dr. Anthony Fauci
sources.summary: C-SPAN/YouTube video of a heated Rand Paul–Fauci exchange on gain-of-function. Video skipped under scrape policy.
sources.book_role: Video record of the continuing GoF dispute after the May 2021 hearing.
